subject: model train enthusiasts
one_liner: An online shop for spare model trains, with enough inventory detail to prove you need every one.
brand_voice_notes: Apply the frozen anti-ai-slop skill read at pipelines/codex-v1/skills/anti-ai-slop/SKILL.md. Use plain retail language and a straight face. The collector sincerely intends to sell something; accurate records gradually defeat that intention. Explain technical distinctions through visible examples. Functional labels stay ordinary. Testimonials are fictional accounts of specific transactions. The studio credit reads 'the worst AI studio ever'.
demo_screen_concept: One merchant product-editor screen with navigation for Products, Orders, Customers and Analytics. Products is selected. The editor shows two nearly identical green model locomotives, one with a small side logo and one with a large logo. Initially they share one stock record: Physical stock 2, Personal reserve 1, Available to buy 1. Select 'Add product option', choose 'Logo size', and assign the two models to Small and Large. 'Keep one of each variant' then reserves both, updating the totals to Physical stock 2, Personal reserve 2, Available to buy 0. A storefront preview beside the editor changes from an active Add to cart button to Sold out. 'Publish product' publishes that exact state and displays 'Published: 2 variants, 0 available'. Visitors can reverse the reserve setting and restore availability. Product photographs, inventory quantities and the storefront preview remain visible together; narrow screens stack the editor above the preview.

hero.h1: Open a shop for trains you won't sell.
hero.sub: Siding gives model train collectors a storefront, checkout and inventory tools for selling their spares. Each tiny difference gets its own product option. Somehow, you no longer own any spares.

features.title: Record every variation.
features.blurb: One locomotive has a small side logo. The other has a large one. Add logo size as a product option and reserve one of each for yourself. Your shop now contains two trains and nothing a customer can buy.

features.title: Add a checkout question.
features.blurb: Ask which year the buyer's miniature railway represents. Block the sale of a locomotive introduced in 1978 to anyone modelling 1972. Your first paying customer has been rejected for living in the wrong imaginary year.

features.title: Set a restock level.
features.blurb: Sell a wagon and receive a supplier order suggestion for its replacement pack of six. Approve it after every sale. You've sold four wagons and bought twenty-four; the sales chart gives you four reasons to celebrate.

testimonials.quote: I entered 38 duplicates. Once I'd recorded the different logos and roofs, I needed one of every version. I sent the shop link to the club anyway. Three people asked when I would have stock.
testimonials.name: Martin Ellis
testimonials.title: Locomotive collector; accounts clerk

testimonials.quote: A buyer selected 1972 and the checkout refused his diesel. He bought it elsewhere and sent me a video of it running on his miniature railway. I replied with the locomotive's introduction date.
testimonials.name: Helen Ward
testimonials.title: Club layout builder; retired surveyor

testimonials.quote: I sold four wagons at the exhibition and approved four replacement packs on my phone. Twenty-four wagons arrived on Tuesday. My wife asked how the clear-out went, so I showed her the sales graph.
testimonials.name: Clive Mercer
testimonials.title: Weekend exhibition seller; warehouse supervisor

observations.behavior: Collectors call items duplicates until selling requires them to examine the differences.
observations.mechanic: Product options separate visible variations, while personal reserves remove a copy of each from sellable inventory.
observations.consequence: Careful catalogue work proves that every supposed spare is essential. The collector pays to operate a fully stocked shop with nothing available.

observations.behavior: Enthusiasts want other people to practise the hobby correctly and will sacrifice a practical benefit to enforce accuracy.
observations.mechanic: Checkout questions and purchase validation compare the buyer's chosen historical year with the model's introduction date.
observations.consequence: A willing buyer fails the seller's history test and purchases elsewhere. The seller continues correcting the buyer after losing the sale.

observations.behavior: Collectors use selling as permission to buy again and treat revenue as evidence that the clear-out is working.
observations.mechanic: Low-stock alerts suggest replenishment in supplier pack quantities, while sales reports celebrate completed orders.
observations.consequence: Each wagon sold authorizes six replacements. Four successful sales add twenty wagons to the collection, and the collector presents the sales graph as proof of progress.

editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: List a spare. Recognizable product visual: a merchant product editor beside its customer-facing storefront preview, with two model locomotives and changing stock availability. Opening hierarchy: Siding identity and small studio credit, headline, explanation, CTA, then a broad working preview. Keep the two physical models and the zero-availability result visible together. Follow with three open feature passages, named customer accounts and a joined software-plan comparison. Proposed artwork one is a catalogue photograph of two nearly identical model locomotives on adjacent lengths of track, with their different logo sizes plainly visible; it explains why a duplicate becomes two essentials. Proposed artwork two shows one outgoing wagon parcel beside four newly opened six-wagon packs on a hobby workbench; it explains how selling enlarges the collection. Individual product photographs populate the editor and storefront rather than serving as decorative backgrounds. Keep quantities, annotations, questions, prices and chart labels in live text. On mobile, put the product editor before the storefront result and keep the publishing action beside its resulting availability. Digest comparison: the comic mechanisms are inventory classification, seller-imposed purchase rejection and replenishment arithmetic. Monthly prices escalate merchant capabilities, and testimonials follow a failed listing, a rejected buyer and a numerically unsuccessful clear-out. Mobile opening: use compact hero spacing, a 38px headline (34px at 360px and below), 16px explanation and a two-column CTA/helper row so recognizable locomotive photography appears within the opening at 390px and 320px. Preserve the complete editor/storefront preview, readable variant captions and single-column model bays at 320px.

references.reference: Model railway exhibition trade stands with stacked locomotive boxes, sample track and small price slips
references.cues: Compact stock labels, orderly rows of boxed models, burgundy display cloth and close inspection of individual objects.
references.application: Use burgundy for the identity and primary actions, cool pale gray for working surfaces, and restrained signal yellow for selected stock. Align products and prices in catalogue rows. Photograph actual miniature models at table height so their scale is clear.

references.reference: Railway Modeller layout photography and model railway exhibition guidebooks
references.cues: Detailed miniature scenes, practical captions, clear section headings and dense but orderly hobby information.
references.application: Pair Roboto Slab headings with IBM Plex Sans body text and controls. Use IBM Plex Mono sparingly for stock identifiers and quantities. Present photographs with readable captions and generous inspection space. Keep decorative railway scenery within photography.

references.reference: Model locomotive box-end labels and fitted storage trays
references.cues: Repeated rectangular compartments, precise model identifiers and packaging that makes each small distinction worth recording.
references.application: Use aligned image bays and label strips for variants, with one shared inventory total beneath them. Carry the same proportions into the plan comparison and product editor without turning every paragraph into a box.

audience_design.landing_application: Build a model railway dealer's catalogue with burgundy #642E3B, signal yellow #E5B64C, cool gray #E7E9E7, white #FFFFFF and charcoal #242D2A. Use slab-serif headlines, readable sans-serif explanations and tightly aligned catalogue information. The broad merchant preview supplies the opening's main visual. Supporting photography examines model differences and collection growth. Alternate open editorial passages with ordered product rows; reserve compartment framing for objects and inventory. On mobile, tighten the introduction and place the primary action beside its helper text to bring the existing locomotive preview into the opening without clipping or hiding catalogue content.
audience_design.demo_application: Retain the source service's merchant navigation, central product form, inventory controls, publish action and storefront preview. Apply the catalogue typography, burgundy controls, yellow selection state and model-box image proportions at a quieter density. Show model photographs large enough to compare their logos. Keep all stock changes and publishing feedback explicit, with the same state represented in the editor and customer-facing preview.

design_direction.style: Model railway dealer catalogue: burgundy exhibition cloth, slab-serif headings, cool-gray fitted object bays and precise box-end stock labels.

palette.name: Exhibition Burgundy, Signal Yellow and Tray Gray

fonts.pairing: Host-approved Roboto Slab and IBM Plex Sans; bundled Financial Trust pairing supplies readable Plex UI hierarchy, with Roboto Slab catalogue headings per audience brief.

design_direction.archetype: Product-led merchant software catalogue: compact proposition above broad product-editor/storefront preview, open editorial features, two composed graphic spreads, customer accounts and joined plan comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms color changes and explicit user-triggered quantity updates. No ambient animation. Reduced motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left-aligned headline and explanation share an opening row; CTA leads straight to product editing. Broad paired train editor and storefront immediately below. Object bays borrow fitted storage trays. Artwork appears after product demonstration. At 760px and below editor precedes storefront in one column.
design_direction.design_review: Compared all seven entries in supplied recent digest. No matching tuple. Storage-tray framing shares hobby practicality but differs from Bare through burgundy slab type, miniature railway imagery and stock availability mechanics. Logo turnout and boxed-model motif differ from reunion book/cursor, cabinets, furniture tags, lightsticks, geese, lifting strap and huddle. Library museum-catalogue recommendation contributes object inspection and open editorial composition; oil-painting hero, vibrant youth defaults and recommended Rubik are rejected in favor of approved audience and product-first workflow.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: A railway siding takes a vehicle out of circulation. The custom turnout mark turns that physical action into personal reserved stock. Burgundy exhibition-stand identity and signal-yellow held wagon support a model dealer catalogue, distinct from recent pet mascots and publication identities.

logo.concept: Accepted Gemini direction A: burgundy parallel rails diverge into a holding siding with a yellow held wagon beside bespoke, correctly spelled Siding slab lettering. Direction B integrated rail is less distinct at icon size.
logo.clear_space: At least half the symbol height around the lockup; crop exports include clear margins.
logo.placement: Landing navigation and footer, demo chrome; isolated icon favicon on both pages

items.prompt: Design a finished original logo lockup for the fictional merchant software brand "Siding" for model railway collectors. Exact text Siding, correctly spelled, no other text. Direction A: custom confident slab-serif wordmark, not a stock font, beside an original compact railway turnout symbol: two parallel burgundy rails diverge into a short holding siding with a small yellow rectangular wagon/held-stock segment. Meaning is keeping a model out of circulation. Symbol on LEFT occupying about one quarter width, wordmark RIGHT. Strong simple silhouette that works at 24px. Color burgundy #642E3B, one signal yellow #E5B64C element, perfectly flat background #E7E9E7. Broad horizontal lockup centered with ample but not excessive whitespace. Railway exhibition dealer catalogue identity. No enclosing rounded square, no initials badge, no shopping bag, no existing railway logo, no mockup, no board, no texture, no shadows, no watermark. Return the actual finished mark and wordmark only.
items.verdict: Accepted direction A. Correct spelling, clear bespoke slab letterforms and open turnout silhouette. Cropped clear space, faithfully normalized flat colors and removed background for flexible contrast.

items.transformation: Same accepted lockup and alpha, recolored uniformly burgundy #642E3B.
Isolated original turnout symbol, centered in transparent square and resized to 192px.
items.verdict: Turnout retains distinctive divergence and yellow held segment.
